Somos uma equipe de seis participantes, com habilidades em pesquisa, comunicação, organização, desenvolvimento web e produção audiovisual. Temos interesse em tecnologia, ciência e exploração espacial.

Nosso objetivo é desenvolver um museu espacial digital e interativo sobre equipamentos deixados em missões na Lua e em Marte.

Valorizamos a criatividade, a colaboração e a troca de conhecimentos. Buscamos agregar habilidades em programação, design, pesquisa científica e análise de dados.
summary:
Beyond the Mission is an interactive educational platform that explores humanity’s legacy in space through the equipment and artifacts left behind during space exploration. Inspired by NASA’s challenge “Abandoned but Not Forgotten,” the project brings together stories of missions to the Moon and Mars, while also exploring humanity’s journey into deep space.

The website features an interactive mission discovery map, an exploration archive, educational videos, a knowledge quiz, and a built-in Space Guide that helps visitors learn about space missions and their historical significance. Information is connected to NASA’s public archives and educational resources.

Our goal is to make space history more accessible, engaging, and meaningful. By sharing the stories behind these forgotten artifacts, we aim to preserve their scientific and historical importance, encourage curiosity, and inspire future generations to value humanity’s achievements in space exploration.
details:
Project Details – Beyond the Mission

Beyond the Mission is an interactive educational website designed to preserve and share the stories of space exploration artifacts left behind during missions to the Moon and Mars. Inspired by NASA’s “Abandoned but Not Forgotten” challenge, the project transforms historical and scientific information into an accessible and engaging digital experience.

The platform allows users to explore an archive of space missions and artifacts, discover locations through an interactive map, watch educational videos, test their knowledge through a 12-question quiz, and use the Space Guide to learn more about space exploration. These features make complex information easier to understand and encourage visitors to explore the history behind each mission.

The main benefit of the project is making space history more accessible, especially for students, educators, and anyone interested in science and technology. Its intended impact is to encourage scientific curiosity, promote space education, and preserve awareness of the historical and scientific value of equipment left beyond Earth.

The website was developed as a software project using HTML (33%), CSS (54%), and JavaScript (13%). Codex supported the development process, GitHub was used for code management and version control, and Render was used exclusively for website hosting and deployment.

The creative approach combines storytelling, interactive learning, visual exploration, and educational resources in a single platform. The team considered accessibility, usability, clear communication, and engagement when designing the experience, aiming to transform forgotten space equipment into meaningful stories that connect past missions with future generations.
